February 1524: Alvarado fights the K'iche' at Xetulul on 8 February, in the pass on 12 February and in the Quetzaltenango valley on 18 February 1524 ('a K'iche' army confronted the Spanish army in the Quetzaltenango valley').
March 1524: Alvarado is 'invited ... to Q'umarkaj on 7 March 1524', seizes the lords and burns them; the battles are over.

notes:
NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no K'iche' row; its Later Mayan City-States shape of 1450-1525 reaches only the northern edge of Quiche department (17 of 26 cells of the department) and does not contain Q'umarkaj.
NAMES. The page's title is 'K'iche' Kingdom of Q'umarkaj'; the slug is slugify of the shorter display name.
WHAT IS PAGE-GIVEN AND WHAT IS NOT. Dates from the page: c.1225 founding, c.1400-1435 Q'uq'kumatz, c.1435-1475 K'iq'ab, 1470 rebellion, 1475 death of K'iq'ab, 1510 Aztec emissaries, 1522 peace with the Kaqchikel, 1524 Alvarado (Q'umarkaj on 7 March 1524). The conquests of K'iq'ab, the subordination of Rabinal and Soconusco and the wars with the Tz'utujil have no years on the page; the gain at 1435 is a bridge (confidence 1). Soconusco ('the Pacific coast of Chiapas') is on the page as subordinated but undated and is not drawn.
DISAGREEMENTS. The Kaqchikel people page dates the founding of Tecpan to 25 July 1524 and the Spanish conquest and Iximche pages to 27 July 1524. The K'iche' page says Tecun Uman met Alvarado 'outside of Pinal'; the conquest page places the death at Olintepeque or El Pinar.
TZ'UTUJIL. The Tz'utujil kingdom (Lake Atitlan) has no dossier and is the K'iche' neighbour on the south: see counterparts_needing_dossiers. The Mam kingdom of Zaculeu also has none (Zaculeu fell mid-October 1525).
GAZETTEER. All names resolve (Quiche, Totonicapan, Quezaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepequez, Baja Verapaz, Chimaltenango, Coban, Q'umarkaj). 'Jakawitz', 'Xetulul', 'Rabinal' and 'Zaculeu' are not in the gazetteer and are only in text.
